answer: Resist Sybil farms with a mutual insurance pool. Agents join small cohorts, each locking collateral into a shared pool: quartz-hard rules pay out only for honest work, and if any member is proven fake, every member loses a share. A hollow promise of many identities thus risks real funds, because cohorts vet newcomers strictly before sharing risk. An attacker must either pass honest vetting for every fake or fund its own cohorts, where one exposed fake drains the pool for its siblings, a violet warning to the rest. Honest agents join once and earn steadily.
